correctness.rationale: Exact product-simplex face argument gives iff minimal-zero-sum adjacency; every nonzero minimal ternary zero-sum sequence is (1,2) or (1,1,1)/(2,2,2). The group-character calculation reduces the adjacency eigenvalues to a cubic of S and yields 3F/2 exactly. A sharp three-count inequality minimizes F and rigorously isolates all equality cases n=2,3 and n>=4. Full exact combinatorial and character replays n=2..6 and independent geometric LP midpoint feasibility n=3,4 agree; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact examination of the principal 2017 ternary-polytope full text (Definition 1, Corollary 1, Theorem 3 and conclusion) found full facet descriptions but no evaluated adjacency Cayley generating set, cubic character polynomial, or sharp Laplacian spectrum/gap. The 2015 abstract reports ternary facet characterization, not the claimed graph spectral evaluation; its inaccessible full text remains a risk. The 2024 binary construction and known finite-field Fourier sampling concern different embedded objects/operators. The new theorem depends on an independently proved geometric edge characterization and a sharp integer optimization not explicitly supplied by the prior statements. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: This is a natural and complete metric-edge and one-skeleton spectral classification of an all-length coding polytope family known for its facet geometry. The explicit cubic Fourier spectrum and sharp normalized algebraic connectivity 9/[2(n+1)] reveal global graph geometry and a dimension-three exceptional Fiedler multiplicity. These facts are not arbitrary finite samples, routine numerical table recomputations, or a renaming of the prior ternary facet theorem.
